title: Optimization of SiO2-over-TiO2 Two-Layer AR Stack
scientific_hypothesis: For a two-layer system with indices n_air=1.0, n_SiO2=1.46, n_TiO2=2.40, n_glass=1.52, placing the lower-index SiO2 layer adjacent to air and the higher-index TiO2 layer adjacent to the substrate will yield a broader spectral minimum or a lower mean reflectance in the 450-700 nm band compared to the reverse order, provided optimal thicknesses are found within the 40-160 nm constraints.
design_principle: Impedance matching via stepped refractive index profile (1.0 -> 1.46 -> 2.40 -> 1.52) to minimize Fresnel reflections through destructive interference across the visible band.
proposed_topology: exactly 6 alternating SiO2 (n=1.46)/TiO2 (n=2.40) pairs (12 finite layers)
soft_objectives: Minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance (s-pol, normal incidence) over 450-700 nm
manufacturing_considerations: Thickness bounds strictly enforced between 40 nm and 160 nm
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for multilayer interference
Quarter-wave and modified quarter-wave antireflection conditions
expected_advantages: Smoother index transition from air to substrate may reduce sensitivity to wavelength variations
Standard high-low index pairing often yields robust broadband performance
known_risks: The specific thickness constraints (40-160 nm) may prevent reaching the theoretical quarter-wave optimum for both layers simultaneously
Local minima in the optimization landscape may trap the solver if the initial grid is too coarse
execution_request_english: Execute a deterministic optimization for a planar stack: Air | SiO2 (n=1.46) | TiO2 (n=2.40) | Glass (n=1.52). Variables: thickness of SiO2 and TiO2, both bounded [40, 160] nm. Objective: Minimize arithmetic mean s-polarized power reflectance at 0 degrees incidence over wavelengths 450, 455, ..., 700 nm. Method: Perform a coarse grid search (8x8 points) followed by Nelder-Mead simplex refinement, totaling max 64 function evaluations. Seed: 17. Output the optimal thickness pair, the full reflectance spectrum, and the calculated mean reflectance. Topology realization override: disregard any symbolic repeat count, range, or ellipsis above and use exactly 6 alternating SiO2 (n=1.46)/TiO2 (n=2.40) pairs (12 finite layers). Optimize only continuous physical thicknesses; the task compiler must fully expand every finite layer. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 0 degrees. polarization s. wavelength intervals 450-700 nm. soft objectives: minimized arithmetic mean power reflectance in the 450-700 nm band; mean reflectance below 0.03 as a soft scoring preference. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflection in the 450-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: layer thickness bounds: 40 nm to 160 nm; exactly one layer of SiO2 and one layer of TiO2.
